title: Concurrent policy snapshots triggered opaque tenant region reassignment
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Summary: Multiple tenants observed sudden increases in latency and errors when inference requests were routed to on-prem/private variants in EU regions instead of hosted US variants. Pager duty alerted at 2026-03-10 02:14 UTC for a spike in 5xxs and token-level latency on the hosted front doors. Initial mitigation routed traffic via emergency override but we still saw ~12% requests misrouted for several minutes. This ticket tracks investigation, fix, rollout, and postmortem.
reproduction_steps: Simulate rapid policy updates: create two policy snapshots (A and B) that differ in region preferences for tenant T (A: us-west priority, B: eu-private only).
Trigger concurrent policy push from control-plane (two nodes) to routing-cache layer to reproduce non-atomic apply ordering.
Send steady traffic from tenant T and observe routing decisions and telemetry (route_tags, resolved_variant, decision_timestamp).
Inspect routing-cache logs for interleaved snapshot IDs and in-flight decision metadata.
symptoms: Customers reported increased tail latency (+200ms median for affected requests), elevated 5xx rate for chat completion endpoints, and support escalations from two enterprise customers on Dedicated plans. Visible in Console as sudden shift in per-region served tokens and spike in cross-region network egress for private-hosted tenants.
root_cause: Race in the policy apply path: when control-plane publishes back-to-back policy snapshots, routing-cache applied the newer snapshot for new evaluations but a background reconcile loop mutated per-tenant affinity state without version checks. In-flight requests evaluated decision using stale affinity pointers that had been overwritten by an asynchronous reconcile, causing a window where some requests resolved to EU private variants while others used the intended US hosted variant. Additionally there was no per-decision snapshot id metadata persisted to the request trace, making debugging and fallback selection ambiguous.
mitigation: Short-term: added an emergency guard in routing-cache to reject non-monotonic snapshot applies (reject an incoming snapshot if its base-version doesn't match), and enabled a tenant-level sticky override for affected tenants to force US-hosted preference. We pushed a temporary feature-flag to rate-limit control-plane snapshot churn for high-traffic tenants.
fix: Implement atomic snapshot apply with version checks and per-decision snapshot_id annotation. Update reconcile loop to be idempotent and use compare-and-swap semantics on affinity pointers. Add unit/integration tests that simulate concurrent snapshot publishes and in-flight request evaluation. Also add telemetry emitting resolved_snapshot_id for every decision so we can trace misroutes in the future.
deployment_plan: 1) Merge PR that implements CAS-based apply and decision-tagging behind a runtime flag. 2) Deploy to staging and run synthetic snapshot-concurrency tests. 3) Canary deploy to low-traffic region for 2 hours while monitoring misroute, latency, and 5xx. 4) Roll to primary regions if green. 5) Flip runtime flag for all clusters. Expected rollout duration: 4 hours.
rollback_plan: If misroutes spike after deploy, rollback by reverting runtime flag to prior behavior (which re-enables previous non-atomic apply). Immediately re-enable tenant-level sticky overrides to force hosted routes and coordinate with SRE to mitigate backlog.
post_deploy_monitoring: track: routing.misroute.rate by tenant and region
console alert: per-tenant cross-region egress > baseline
notes: Customer comms: sent interim update to affected customers on 2026-03-11 stating we had isolated the cause and applied temporary overrides. Next update scheduled after canary. Action items: coordinate with Solutions to validate tenant sticky override doesn't violate Dedicated isolation contracts; schedule follow-up postmortem with cross-functional attendees (SRE, Control Plane, Routing, Customer Success).
